specialRules.ruleFull: Every warrior of the warband, hired swords excepted, hates Dark Elves.
Every Elf of the warband spots hidden enemies from twice his Initiative in inches.
In multiplayer games the warband may never ally with a warband of a chaotic nature (Possessed, Skaven, Beastmen, Dark Elves and the like).
The warband may hire any hired sword who isn't chaotic or evil (no Skaven, Possessed, Beastmen, Dark Elves, Undead and the like).
The starred prices (Ithilmar weapons at 2 × price, Ithilmar Armour at 60 gc) are for a new warband, with no roll to find them. Later the warband pays the usual price and rolls to find them as usual.
Only one Hero of the warband may have Seeker.
Warriors within 6" of the Hunt Master may use his Leadership when taking Leadership tests.
A Waywatcher may shoot while hidden. After he shoots roll a D6: on a 5+ he stays hidden.
While a Waywatcher is hidden, every enemy model must pass an extra Initiative test to spot him.
The Forest Mage is a wizard and casts from the Woodland Incantations.
When more than one Deepwood Scout shoots at the same target, they have +1 to their injury rolls.

specialSkillsList.name: Elven Luck
specialSkillsList.description: Once per game the Wood Elf may re-roll any failed roll.

specialSkillsList.name: Infiltration (Wood Elves of Athel Loren)
specialSkillsList.description: The Wood Elf is always set up last, anywhere out of the enemy's sight. If both sides have infiltrators, each rolls a D6 and the lowest sets up first.

flags.what: A Wood Elf warband needs at least 3 models: our templates hold no minimum, so it is not imported.
The maximum is the rulebook's (p121), so the Elves take our Elf race.

The skill table's ticks are a symbol font, read from where the text layer places them: Hunt Master Combat, Shooting, Academic, Speed, Special; Waywatcher Combat, Shooting, Speed, Special; Forest Mage Shooting, Academic, Speed, Special.

The starred prices are for starting only (a warband rule). The footnote also says "Heroes only", yet the Scout list, which only henchmen use, has the same starred lines: both lists keep them, with no note.

List prices as printed: Elven Cloak 75 gc (ours 100; the PDF's own entry 75+D6x10, Rare 12), Ithilmar Armour 60 gc (ours 90), Hunting Arrows 35 gc (ours 25), Elven Wine 50 gc (the PDF's entry 50+3D6, Rare 10).

Elven Runestones (50+2D6 gc, Rare 11, Forest Mage only) and the Familiar (20+D6 gc, Rare 8, spell-users only) are on no list: they are special equipment, both ours, the Forest Mage's (the only spell-user).
The Leader rule says "within 6" of the Protector of the Hunt": read as the Hunt Master, who leads.
"Bought in groups of 1-5" stands over the henchmen: Deepwood Scouts and Glade Guard come in groups of 1-5.

The special skills are a new group, Wood Elves of Athel Loren. Fey is our Fey; Excellent Sight is our Unblinking Eye (and also a warband rule for every Elf); Seeker is our Resource Hunter, word for word in effect, its "only one Elven Hero" a warband rule. Elven Luck is named apart (our Luck re-rolls any roll, theirs a failed one), and so is Infiltration (theirs has no 12" limit).
Woodland Incantations is a new lore. Lyrics of Feral Infatuation gives no range or duration, and Song of the Sun names no test ("must make a test"): both are kept as printed.
